summary: The diff implements %TypedArray%.prototype.reduce in the stub's file, following the spec steps in order. ValidateTypedArray (step 2) runs before the callable check (step 4), and the empty-with-no-initial-value TypeError (step 5) comes after it. Length is captured once (step 3). Initial-value presence is tested via args.get(1) (step 8). The k increment in the else branch comes after the first TypedArrayGetElement (step 9). The loop (step 10) gets kValue before the Call, passes «accumulator, kValue, 𝔽(k), obj» with undefined this, propagates the Call error with `?`, and increments k. Nothing is special-cased, no made-up values, no swallowed errors. The only renamed item is new_target to _new_target, which is needed because the parameter is now unused. The 6 remaining failures are BigInt not-implemented errors, which is an honest limitation.
notes_for_next_attempt: Looks spec-faithful; no required changes from this review. Two things to confirm before landing, neither of which is a defect I can see in the diff: (1) Check that push_root's return value is the stack mark that pop_roots expects. The loop does `let mark = agent.push_root(accumulator); agent.push_root(k_value); ... agent.pop_roots(mark);`. If push_root returns the length after the push, one root leaks per iteration. A GC-stress run (KAHVI_GC_STRESS=1) would show this. (2) typed_array_get_element returns a plain Value with no Result, so BigInt failures surface elsewhere. Confirm that helper does not hide a BigInt error by returning undefined. The remaining 6 BigInt test failures are a pre-existing engine limitation and are acceptable.
